lena: Heads-up — partner pushed a gist that includes a KMS‑wrapped Vault ciphertext. Looks like staging creds but treat as potential exfil. Link: https://gist.github.com/partner/example (saw at 02:25 UTC). cc @tom @jess

 tom: Thanks. Which key/version did they reference? Any sign it's prod?

 lena: The blob references `projects/partner-proj/locations/global/keyRings/partner-kr/cryptoKeys/partner-key/cryptoKeyVersions/5`. The vault path in their notes is `secret/data/partner/staging`. From the gist context it seems staging, but could be copied. I did a quick IAM check — partner SA had a cross-project grant to use our wrapping key (granted last year). Not sure on audit events yet.

 jess: I'll query audit logs for KMS Decrypt/AsymmetricDecrypt calls and any IAM changes. Searching for `methodName:\"Decrypt\" OR methodName:\"asymmetricDecrypt\"` in stackdriver. Also check if version 5 is still primary.

 sec-bot: INC-2026-032 created: \"Partner gist — KMS-wrapped Vault blob exposure\". Assigned to @lena, priority P2.

 aaron: Quick notes on rotation approach: ideally do a KMS rewrap (server-side) so we don't have to materialize plaintext. Options: 1) create a new key version on the same CryptoKey and call a re-encrypt-like operation if provider supports it; 2) if not possible, create new key version and perform decrypt+encrypt inside a secure ephemeral VM with no logging (avoid writing plaintext to disk). We also need to rotate Vault transit/wrapping config or re-write the wrapped value.

 lena: Audit log snippet I grabbed: `\"protoPayload.methodName\":\"Decrypt\"` from principal `partner-sa@partner-proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com` at 2026-03-18T02:17:11Z (single call). Gist commit was 02:25Z. So likely they pulled the ciphertext then pushed it to gist. Treat as exfil.

 tom: Action items: rotate wrapping key (or at least create new version), rewrap affected ciphertexts, revoke partner SA cross-project grant temporarily, and sweep Vault for secrets that reference that key. Who owns the Vault write perms? @jess?

 jess: I'll own the Vault side. Plan: 1) enumerate `secret/partner/*` entries, 2) for each entry referencing `partner-key` record metadata, 3) in a maintenance window rewrap to new key version and write back to Vault with new metadata and rotation tag. Schedule 30m out. I'll also prepare rollback steps.

 lena: I'll open an emergency IAM change request to remove the cross-project grant and notify partner (they should expect ~1h disruption). Aaron — can you run the rewrap test on staging only first?

 aaron: Yup. I'll do a dry-run on a copy of the ciphertext in our test project. Also recommend exporting KMS audit logs to BigQuery with a filter for `resource.labels.key_ring=partner-kr` so we keep longer retention while we investigate.

 tom: Don't forget RBAC for Vault readers: rotate any tokens/service accounts that can read `secret/partner/staging`. Add temporary deny for partner's service account on the key in IAM. Add a fallback policy: keep previous key/version available for 10 minutes post-rotation to allow traffic to failover, then revoke.

 jess: Runbook snippet (will refine to avoid plaintext spills):
```
# emergency-rotate-partner-key (staging only)
# 1) create new key version
gcloud kms keys versions create --key=partner-key --keyring=partner-kr --location=global --project=our-proj
# 2) test rewrap (server-side preferred). If not possible, run ephemeral VM decrypt+encrypt with strict logging disabled
# 3) update vault secret
vault kv put secret/partner/staging value=@cipher_v2.bin metadata.kms_version=6
# 4) tag secret with rotation: rotated_by=eng-security rotated_at=2026-03-18T03:00:00Z
```
I'll post the full commands + CI-safe script in ~10m.

 lena: I'll loop in legal and partnerships for the external notification and SLA implications. Partner notified via secure channel. Update this thread with progress. :thumbsup:
